name: How do I stop a guest bathroom from feeling cramped after remodeling?

mainEntity.name: What design choices prevent a guest bathroom from feeling smaller after a remodel?
mainEntity.text: What design choices prevent a guest bathroom from feeling smaller after a remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A guest bathroom feels cramped when it has too many visual breaks, oversized fixtures, or a layout that interrupts circulation. To make the room feel larger, use a compact but functional vanity, a larger mirror, and consistent finishes that help the eye move smoothly through the space. Glass shower enclosures often work better than heavy curtains or opaque partitions because they open the room visually. Lighter colors can help, but the real trick is balance: too many small patterns or competing materials can make a bathroom feel busy rather than airy. Storage should be built in carefully so it does not protrude into the room. Good lighting matters too, especially in smaller baths common in older Los Angeles homes. A remodel that preserves clear walking paths and reduces clutter almost always feels more spacious than one that simply adds more features.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use a lighter palette, large mirror, glass shower enclosure, compact vanity, and simple tile pattern to reduce visual clutter. Keep the layout open, avoid oversized fixtures, and maximize storage without bulking up the room. Better lighting and a clear floor line also make the space feel larger.
